To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
draxin and TSUKUSHI are essential for the formation and maintenance of the forebrain commissural axon tracts.
the combined guidance functions of draxin, a secreted repulsive axon growth inhibitor and Tsukushi, a secreted extracellular matrix molecule are essential for fore-brain commissure formation.

draxin/ TSUKUSHI double heterozygosity leads to the formation of a significantly higher number of mice with corpus callosum malformations and agenesis in the anterior commissures than draxin or TSUKUSHI single heterozygosity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic and molecular mechanisms underlying the formation of forebrain commissural projections and the genetic interaction between draxin and a secreted molecule TSK in this process.
the identification of novel axon guidance molecules and their genetic interaction in the developing forebrain.
the molecular mechanisms of axon guidance, and the results of our study will be important in understanding the molecular mechanism of forebrain commissurization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

draxin and tsukushi are both required for the normal formation of the forebrain commissural system and that their combinatorial guidance activity is essential for the normal development of the forebrain.
draxin and tsukushi are essential combinatorial guidance molecules for the formation of forebrain commissural axons.
draxin and tsukushi are essential combinatorial guidance molecules for the formation of the CC and the AC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
draxin and/or TSK function in the formation of forebrain commissural axons by inhibiting the outgrowth of commissural axon tips and by providing repulsive signals to the axon tips.
the combined guidance activity of draxin/ TSK is essential for the development of forebrain commissural axons.
draxin and the secreted molecule Tsukushi are both required for the formation of the corpus callosus, and Tsukushi also regulates anterior olfactory and cortical commissures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
draxin and tsukushi (TSk) are essential for fore brain commissure formation and that their combined guidance activities are important in this process.
the combinatorial guidance function of draxin/ TSK is essential for the proper development of the forebrain commissural system.
draxin and the secreted SLRP, TSK, have additive functions in the regulation of forebrain commissural axon guidance.
